version: LOCK 66 V1 (9 Nov 2026) - the scholar's notebook, chapter 3: Giving and wealth
builds_on: LOCK 3 (page 1, read with Idris), LOCK 34 runner, LOCK 51 (the last page). Every reference checked on sunnah.com; the game never shows the reference.

words.find_kicker: The scholar's notebook · a page found
words.find_title: A page in the scholar's hand
words.read_button: Read the scholar's page with Idris
words.story: Idris turns back through the pages. “{t}”

chapter.title: Giving and wealth
chapter.story: When his father died he gave away half the shop to the bookbinders who had no tools of their own.

pages.saying: It is better to take a rope, gather firewood and sell it than to beg from people who may give or refuse.
pages.idris: Work is never shameful. Asking when you can work is harder on the soul.
pages.found: Ghazi found a page lining an old hat bought from a pedlar.

pages.saying: Be mindful of Allah and He will protect you; when you ask, ask Allah; if the whole world gathered to help or harm you, it could do only what Allah has already written.
pages.idris: The pen has lifted and the ink is dry. So stop being afraid.
pages.found: Wahb hands you a loaf wrapped in an old page. “Look at the writing on this.”

pages.saying: From the words of the earlier prophets: if you feel no shame, do as you wish.
pages.idris: Shame is a guard at the door. Don't dismiss it.
pages.found: Amina found a folded page in a crack while mending a wall. “It's in a scholar's hand. You'll know who wants it.”

pages.saying: A man asked for one thing to hold on to. He was told: say 'I believe in Allah', then stand firm.
pages.idris: Believing is the first step. Standing firm is every step after.
pages.found: Children are flying a kite made from an old page. Ghazi buys it from them for a date and gives it to you.

pages.saying: A man asked whether praying, fasting Ramadan and keeping to the lawful would bring him to Paradise, and was told yes.
pages.idris: Simple things done faithfully. Don't make it harder than it is.
pages.found: Wahb found a page pressed inside a second-hand book.

pages.saying: Purity is half of faith; praising Allah fills the scales; prayer is light, charity is proof, patience is brightness.
pages.idris: You saw the women at Birana's well before dawn. Patience is a kind of light.
pages.found: Amina has been using a page to wrap spices and has only just noticed the writing.

pages.saying: Allah says: O My servants, I have forbidden injustice for Myself and made it forbidden between you, so do not wrong one another.
pages.idris: If Allah forbade injustice to Himself, who are we to allow it?
pages.found: Ghazi pulls a damp page from the bottom of a basket and dries it for you.

pages.saying: The poor said the rich take all the reward because they give in charity. He told them: every glorification of Allah is charity, every praise is charity, enjoining good and forbidding wrong is charity.
pages.idris: No one is too poor to give. Some gifts cost nothing but intention.
pages.found: Wahb found a page under a loose floor tile.

pages.saying: Every joint of a person owes a charity every day: making peace between two people, helping a man onto his mount, a good word, every step to prayer, removing harm from the road.
pages.idris: The thorns you moved from the street. Nobody saw. It counted.
pages.found: Amina was given a debt note - and the scholar's page is written on the back of it.

pages.saying: Charity never decreases wealth; Allah raises the one who forgives, and humbles no one who is humble for His sake.
pages.idris: Count your coins after giving. Then count what came back to you another way.
pages.found: Ghazi's little one folded a page into a paper boat. Ghazi dried it out for you.
